participation.context: Set the four-shilling glass against the chair, and listened to the jam.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Brought both sums from the Rose book, and said he had not seen a jam.
participation.name: William Blackwage, Ralph Raye, Richard Hoope

participation.context: Showed the beam, the rope and the jam with a knife and a crust.
participation.name: James Burbage

participation.context: Asked what the chair does when the rope sticks, and kept anyone from trying it at the table.
participation.name: Richard Burbage

participation.context: Stayed for the pork, and said a book has not met a rope.
participation.name: Thomas Pope

participation.context: Said a chair is a chair until someone sits in it. He did not sit in one.
participation.name: Will Kemp

participation.context: Set pork down, and came back for the plates before the talk could finish the dinner.
participation.name: Agnes Tipping

relations.from: William Blackwage, Ralph Raye, Richard Hoope
relations.note: the Rose sum, reported at the table
relations.quote: Henslowe paid his carpenters seven pounds and two shillings for making a throne in the heavens.

story.body: You heard the seven pounds two shillings and the three pounds ten. You set a glass at four shillings against the chair. You let James show the jam on a crust. You did not agree to build anything.

relations.from: William Blackwage, Ralph Raye, Richard Hoope
relations.note: the Rose sum, reported at the table
relations.quote: Henslowe paid his carpenters seven pounds and two shillings for making a throne in the heavens.

title: Heard the throne's price and the new play's price

participation.context: Refused the rope, repeated that the parts are not cast, and kept the castle in the air.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Repeated the two sums and refused to price a barrel.
participation.name: William Blackwage, Ralph Raye, Richard Hoope

participation.context: Named five pound and a lease, and left both as a sentence.
participation.name: James Burbage

participation.context: Looked at you when Pope proposed lowering Kemp, and chose the glass over the chair.
participation.name: Richard Burbage

participation.context: Proposed they lower Kemp, and conceded the sentence.
participation.name: Thomas Pope

participation.context: Asked for a barrel, was refused, and walked out on his feet.
participation.name: Will Kemp

participation.context: Cleared the plates and took the table back.
participation.name: Agnes Tipping

relations.note: Pope would lower him, and the table would not

story.body: You answered Pope and Kemp with a boy and two men, and with a castle that costs nothing to strike. You did not cast a part. You did not give James five pound. You left the chair where Raye had found it.

relations.note: Pope would lower him, and the table would not

title: Answered the five-pound heavens with a castle of air
